citation: Spuhler et al. (2021). Sanitation-system assessment research. Journal of Environmental Management. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2020.111785
description: Santiago is a Julia tool for generating and assessing sanitation-system options, developed by the Santiago sanitation research team at Eawag. It combines available technologies into compatible systems, scores their appropriateness for a specified case and estimates annual material flows with Monte Carlo uncertainty. Inputs are JSON technology and case definitions plus phosphorus, nitrogen, total-solids and water masses. Outputs include system properties, recovery and loss statistics, DataFrames, CSV and JSON exports, with graph visualisation through Graphviz. Coverage is globally configurable and case-specific, with annual mass accounting, not a fixed geographic database. Public source and worked examples are free under AGPL-3.0-or-later. A limitation is that system generation can be computationally intensive, and a capped stochastic search does not guarantee every possible system. Technology properties and local suitability scores require defensible case inputs. Santiago supports sanitation option screening and complements QSDsan (model-qsdsan-quantitative-sustainable-design-sanitation), which represents treatment processes in greater detail. The README cites its sanitation-planning research, including the 2021 assessment paper. No systems were generated or case files downloaded.
